_**Agent (grok-4.6)**_

Your four stories are the right **member** spine. For federation officials I would treat them as half the pitch: they prove the archive is useful to Spieler and Clubs. The other half should prove it is useful to **the BBU itself** — results publication, Meisterschaften, prestige, and history.

The four you listed already map cleanly onto pages that exist:

| # | Story | In-app today |
|---|--------|----------------|
| 1 | Personal stats | `/spieler` (career cards, clubs, highlights, tournament finishes) |
| 2 | Club activities & standings | `/club` + **Mein Club** (`?myClub=`) + Liga scoped to that club |
| 3 | Current league picture | `/liga?season=latest` (all tables) or a named league |
| 4 | League history (Bayernliga) | `/liga` with league set and season `all` — averages, records, points-to-win |

They miss three product surfaces that officials will notice if you skip them: **Turniere**, **Spieltag = Ergebnisliste**, and **Club 300**.

---

## Stories I would add

Keep the set small. Eight stories is a 25-minute live walkthrough; twelve is a website, not a meeting.

**5. “Letzter Spieltag — wie die Ergebnisliste, nur klickbar”**  
This is the comparison they already live in (PDF/Excel). Open a specific week: table, honor scores, team-vs-team, then one scoresheet. The job is not analytics — it is *“can we stop hunting files?”*

**6. “Landesmeisterschaft verstehen”**  
Podium archive → one event (e.g. Nordbayerische) → Gesamtwertung → one KO/Finale round. Federation identity lives here more than in Liga. Your current four stories never leave league play.

**7. “Wer hat den 300er?” (Club 300)**  
Short, memorable, projector-friendly. Shows the app is not only tables. Optionally filter with Mein Club so it feels local.

**8. “Alle Ligen dieser Saison auf einen Blick”**  
Close to your #3, but make it an **ops** story, not a fan story: Sportwart / Ligaausschuss opening `season` without a league. That is the closest thing you have to a federation dashboard. Do not merge it into the Bayernliga history story — different job.

Those four extras cover the dimensions the first four do not: **publication UX, championships, prestige, federation-wide ops**.

Optional ninth if the room is technical or skeptical about data:

**9. “Dieselbe Person über Clubwechsel und 15 Jahre”**  
A known player with several clubs and mixed Liga + Turnier. That is the identity/archive argument: names and EDV-IDs actually join. Skip it if the meeting is purely political; keep it if someone will ask “woher kommen die Daten?”

I would **not** lead with clutch/consistency, heatmaps, or Diagnose. Those are depth for a second meeting. Clubpokal is a named hole — mention it once as coming, do not click `/clubpokal`.

---

## Audience: two layers, one demo

Officials will sit in the room as **Funktionäre**, but they are also Spieler, Eltern, Clubvorstände. The trick is to run **member stories first** (empathy, “this is for our people”) then **switch hat** to federation jobs (publication, Meisterschaft, archive).

A workable order for a live session:

1. Player career (your #1)  
2. Club + Mein Club (your #2)  
3. Current tables, all leagues (your #3 / my #8)  
4. One Spieltag as Ergebnisliste (my #5)  
5. Bayernliga history (your #4)  
6. One Meisterschaft (my #6)  
7. Club 300 closer (my #7)  

That is seven beats, ~3–4 minutes each, plus questions. Home already has curated deep links for several of these; they are labeled as examples, not as stories.

---

## How I would realize it (no new product, at first)

You already have the hard part: **shareable deep links** (`season`, `league`, `week`, `club`, `player_id`, `tournament`, `myClub`, `database`). Home “Beispiele” are a proto-showcase without narration or pacing.

I would **not** start with slides, and I would **not** start with a generic product-tour overlay (highlight the Season dropdown, etc.). Officials do not need a UI tutorial; they need *jobs they recognize*, executed on real pages.

Three layers, in this order of investment:

### 1. Live run-of-show (this week, zero product work)

A one-page script: story title, URL, what you click, one sentence you say, what you do **not** click. Pin seasons and named entities (a well-known Bayernliga club, a player with a clean career, Bayernliga `all` seasons, one championship with a KO). Warm the pages once before the meeting.

This is the highest ROI. The risk is presenter-dependent and “current season” moving under you — so pin `25/26` (or whichever season is complete and flattering) rather than `latest` unless the meeting is mid-season and freshness is the point.

### 2. In-app **Story mode** (the thing to build if you want “interactive in app”)

A thin layer, not a parallel UI:

- Entry: `/` with a “Für Funktionäre” / “Geschichten” strip, or `/showcase`.
- Each story is a **playlist of existing URLs** plus 1–2 sentences of copy (“Du bist Spieler X — Clubs, Turniere, beste Platzierungen”).
- A sticky narrator: story name, beat 2/5, *Weiter* / *Zurück*, *Frei erkunden*.
- *Weiter* just navigates the real route. Filters, charts, tables stay the real product.
- Optional: `?story=player&beat=3` so you can send one link after the meeting.

That reuses what you already designed for Mein Club and home examples. It is interactive without being a fake demo database. People can leave the rails, poke a table, and resume.

What I would avoid in v1: a full Shepherd/Intro.js chrome tour, a separate “demo dataset”, or a kiosk that hides the rest of the nav. Those go stale and look like a different product.

### 3. Self-serve after the meeting

Same stories as cards on Home (grouped by persona: Spieler / Club / Liga / Turnier / Rekorde), plus a short `/warum-bowlyzer` closer. QR on a handout → Story 1. No PDF deck required if Story mode exists; a one-pager of URLs is enough as backup if the room has bad wifi.

---

## Design choices that matter more than widgets

**Pin the cast.** Home currently demos EMAX / Birkner / BK München 3. For BBU officials, pick names they will recognize as *their* sport (Bayernliga club, a Meisterschaft, maybe a women’s event). Avoid Diagnose, Clubpokal placeholder, and empty filter states.

**Mein Club is the personalization trick.** For story 2, set `myClub` once and then hop Liga → Turnier → Spieler so the ribbon does the work. That is more convincing than explaining the filter model.

**Say the gaps out loud once.** No Verein rollup, no Clubpokal, archive not complete before ~2006 / some tournaments missing, no official login or PDF export. That reads as honesty, not as a missing feature list, if you say it after they have seen Spieltag + Meisterschaft + 20 years of Bayernliga.

**Do not sell analytics as the headline.** Federation language is Ergebnisse, Archiv, Nachvollziehbarkeit, Meisterschaften. Clutch and heatmaps are dessert.

**Projector vs phone.** Tables and standings survive a projector; player search and Mein Club feel better if one official follows on a laptop. Story mode with deep links lets both happen.

---

## What I would not add yet

- A slide deck that duplicates the app.  
- Role-based “official mode.” Same public app is the point.  
- Verein-level views just for the meeting.  
- Opening Diagnose in production unless they ask “can we trust this?” — then a *prepared* coverage slide or a single validation screenshot is safer than the full DEV hub.

If you want a next step later, the smallest product increment is: **name the seven stories, freeze their URLs, put them on Home as persona cards with one-line jobs** — that is already interactive, and Story-mode chrome can sit on top when you need a guided meeting.

---

Home is already doing about six jobs. The stories should not become a seventh block on `/`.

Right now the landing page stacks: hero → scale stats → Schnellstart → entity map (sitemap) → 60-second explainers → **Beispiele + letzte Events** → legacy bridge → footer. The Beispiele list is already a proto-showcase: nine unlabeled deep links with no persona and no “why.” Adding seven story cards *next to that* would duplicate it and make the scroll worse.

---

## Put it on its own route

A small index page — something like `/einstieg` or `/rundgang` — with the seven frozen stories. That page can later grow the sticky “Weiter” chrome without touching Home again.

**Home only gets a door**, not the content: one Schnellstart tile or one hero line (“Typische Einstiege”) that jumps there. Same link from `/warum-bowlyzer` (“lieber ausprobieren”) and from a QR / meeting URL.

That matches how you already split jobs:

| Route | Job |
|--------|-----|
| `/` | Orient, search, latest results |
| `/warum-bowlyzer` | Trust, sources, history claim |
| `/glossar` | Vocabulary |
| **new** | **Jobs: “I am X, show me Y”** |

Folding the stories into Warum would mix manifesto and walkthrough and make *that* page too long. Glossar is the wrong metaphor. A query flag on Home (`?showcase=1`) is fine as a presenter trick later, not as the public increment.

---

## Nav: optional, not required

The Start group is already crowded (Übersicht, Warum, Club 300, Glossar). For the federation meeting, **the sendable URL matters more than a sidebar item**. You can ship the page with no new nav entry and still run the session.

If you do add it, I’d rather **replace** something than append:

- Swap the Home Beispiele section for the door, and/or
- Put “Einstieg” in Start and let Warum stay the essay.

Club 300 as a Start item is a prestige destination; a Rundgang is an onboarding destination. They should not sit as equals if the group stays at four items — Einstieg is closer to Warum/Glossar than to Club 300.

---

## Home should get shorter in the same increment

Placement only works if Beispiele go away. Otherwise you have two curated-link lists.

The stories page **absorbs Beispiele**. That is the minimum cut.

If you want `/` actually shorter, the next candidates are the pieces that overlap the new page or the nav:

- **Entity map** — sitemap of pages the sidebar already lists. Stories walk those pages with a job attached. Keeping both is the main reason Home feels long.
- **Explainers** (“Ligaspiel / Turniere in 60 Sekunden”) — domain onboarding; Glossar + the first two Liga/Turnier stories cover this. Could move onto the Einstieg page as a short preamble, or die.
- **Legacy bridge** — already told on Warum.

I would **keep** on Home: hero, compact stats, Schnellstart (Spieler / Club / Mein Club), letzte Events. That is “what is this + do a task + what’s new.” Everything else is either sitemap, tutorial, or demo playlist.

---

## What I would not do

- Cards in the hero (too much for returning users who just want Mein Club / last Spieltag).
- A modal tour from Home (bad for sharing, bad on a projector).
- Putting all seven cards in the sidebar (nav is for destinations, not playlists).
- Hiding the page as DEV-only — then you cannot send it after the meeting.

---

## Naming, because it affects where it *feels* like it lives

“Stories” is our working word; it will look odd in the UI. For BBU I’d lean **Einstieg** or **Typische Einstiege** (job-shaped, not marketing). **Rundgang** is fine for a guided meeting, a bit museum. **Beispiele** is what you already have and is too weak.

URL I’d prefer: `/einstieg` (stable, sendable, not cute). Each card can later become `/einstieg?story=spieler`.

---

**Bottom line:** own page, Home only points at it, Beispiele move there, and use that move to delete duplicate Home sections rather than stacking. Nav can wait until the page exists and you see whether officials and members actually arrive through the sidebar or through the link you send.

Seven stories, frozen examples, real pages:

1. Personal stats — Birkner  
2. Club — EMAX overview, then season 25/26  
3. Current tables — all leagues 25/26  
4. Spieltag as Ergebnisliste — BZOL S1 week 3, then a Bayernliga scoresheet  
5. Bayernliga history — `season=all`  
6. Meisterschaft — season podium → Nordbayerische → Frauen-Finale  
7. Club 300  

On a story, the bar at the top has **Zurück / Weiter**, and **X** to leave the rundgang. If someone clicks away, it says they left the path and offers **Zum Schritt**.

Home lost the Beispiele list, entity map, 60-second explainers, and the legacy bridge. What’s left: hero, stats, Schnellstart, letzte Events.

**01 Spieler** — career (all seasons), then **25/26**.

**02 Club** — Beat 2 looked the same because the club overview ignored `season`. It now has a season control and the matrix/history/KPIs are scoped to that season. Beat 3 is **Mannschaft 1** (`BC EMAX Unterföhring 1`) still on 25/26.

**04 Spieltag** — one path: Saison 25/26 → BayL → Spieltag 2 → BK München 3 → Spiel 1.

**06 Meisterschaft** — full archive first (no season/tournament), then stays on **BM Frauen 25/26**, then Runde 3.

05 and 07 unchanged.

```bash
uv run python -c "
from app.services.club_legends_service import ClubLegendsService
from app.services.club_player_results_service import ClubPlayerResultsService

club = 'BC EMAX Unterfoehring'
# try both spellings
for c in ['BC EMAX Unterfoehring', 'BC EMAX Unterföhring']:
    legends = ClubLegendsService(league_database='db_real_merged')
    alltime = legends.get_club_legends(c)
    season = legends.get_club_legends(c, season='25/26')
    print('CLUB', c, 'resolved alltime', alltime.get('club'), 'season', season.get('club'))
    print(' alltime most_games', [(e['player_name'], e.get('games')) for e in alltime.get('most_games', [])[:3]])
    print(' season  most_games', [(e['player_name'], e.get('games')) for e in season.get('most_games', [])[:3]])
    print(' alltime most_seasons', len(alltime.get('most_seasons', [])), 'season most_seasons', len(season.get('most_seasons', [])))
    results = ClubPlayerResultsService(league_database='db_real_merged')
    t_all = results.get_club_player_results_table(c)
    t_s = results.get_club_player_results_table(c, season='25/26')
    n_all = len(t_all.get('table', {}).get('data') or [])
    n_s = len(t_s.get('table', {}).get('data') or [])
    print(' results rows alltime', n_all, 'season', n_s)
    if n_s:
        row = t_s['table']['data'][0]
        print(' top season row', row.get('player_name'), 'games', row.get('games'), 'avg', row.get('average'), 'membership', row.get('membership_seasons'))
    if n_all:
        row = t_all['table']['data'][0]
        print(' top alltime row', row.get('player_name'), 'games', row.get('games'), 'avg', row.get('average'), 'membership', row.get('membership_seasons'))
    break
"

```

import pandas as pd
from data_access.schema import Columns
from data_access.text_norm import normalize_unicode_label
from pathlib import Path

p = Path('database/data/player_stats_merged_plus_tournaments.parquet')
print('exists', p.exists(), p)
df = pd.read_parquet(p)
print('cols', list(df.columns)[:20])
print('rows', len(df))
club_col = Columns.club if Columns.club in df.columns else None
print('club col', club_col, 'season', Columns.season in df.columns)
if club_col:
    clubs = df[club_col].astype(str)
    mask = clubs.str.contains('EMAX', case=False, na=False)
    sub = df.loc[mask]
    print('emax rows', len(sub))
    print('sample clubs', sub[club_col].dropna().astype(str).unique()[:10])
    if Columns.season in sub.columns:
        print('seasons', sorted(sub[Columns.season].astype(str).str.strip().unique())[-8:])
        s25 = sub[sub[Columns.season].astype(str).str.strip().eq('25/26')]
        print('25/26 rows', len(s25))
"

Club legends and the player results table were still loading **all-time** club stats, even with `season=25/26` in the URL.

They now use that season:

- **Club-Legenden** — only league games in 25/26 (career categories like “Meiste Saisons” / “Beste Saisons” are hidden)
- **Spielerergebnisse** — one row per player for that season, not career totals

On BC EMAX Unterföhring that means 25/26 legends start at ~44 games (Pirzer), not 537 (Blasits), and the table drops from 99 players to 23.

The React page already shows the season hint. **Restart Flask** (`start.sh`) so the API picks this up — the process that is running still serves the old all-time payload.

_**Agent (grok-4.6)**_

Those Diagnose pages were failing in local because Vite never proxied `/pipeline/*` to Flask — the UI got the SPA HTML instead of JSON and stayed on “Laden…”. They were also hidden in production (`import.meta.env.DEV`).

Both are fixed:

- **Local delivery:** `/pipeline` is proxied like `/league`. Turnier-Übersicht, Validierung, and Datenpipeline now load their reports (coverage matrix, 394 Liga rows, publish manifest).
- **Production:** Diagnose is in the sidebar and `/diagnose/*` routes again, instead of redirecting home. After the next SPA deploy they will be reachable on the live site too.

Filesystem paths on Datenpipeline stay redacted in the container; only the pages themselves are public again.

---

_**User**_

finally, we need an overhaul of the club 300 page. 
be creative in presenting the info in a better way, but make sure we see:
- who got how many 300s
- a list with every 300 noted down

---

_**Agent (grok-4.6)**_

I’ll start from the current Club 300 page and the Stadium design system, then redesign it so both the per-player 300 counts and the full game list stay visible.
